# com.noblemaster.lib.data.DateTime - a date/time value wrapped around a long millisecond count.
# Evidence is on the declaration/body plus the format tokens it substitutes:
#   static a/b = DateTime.a(-1000000,..)/.a(1000000,..) bounds -> MIN / MAX
#   c = -62135596800000L, the millisecond value of year 1, used as a BC/AD floor -> yearOneMillis
#   f = the stored instant in ms -> timeMillis
#   g/h = cached java.util.Date for the local (r) and utc (s) views -> localDate / utcDate
# Constructors/setters: c(int*7) uses Date.UTC -> setUtc; d(int*7) uses a local Date -> setLocal;
#   static a(int*7) calls setUtc -> create; static b(int*7) calls setLocal -> createLocal.
# Getters come in two families feeding the two cached Dates: c()/e()/g()/i()/k()/m()/o() read r()
#   getMillisecond; d()/f()/h()/j()/l()/n()/p() read s() (utc) with the Utc suffix.
# Other members: a()=now, a(long)=setTimeMillis, b()=getMillis, b(int)=addDays (24*3600*1000 ms),
#   private a(String,7 ints)=formatImpl (substitutes yyyy MM dd hh mm ss SSS),
#   e(int*7)=validate (the range checks), q()=copy (clone target). No reflection/serialization
#   touches DateTime (only UnitType does), so renaming is safe.
